title: Minimum coin count for coin change
summary: Illustrate an optimal coin selection that makes target amount 11.
context: Coin change provides 3 coin denominations coins = [1, 2, 5] in unlimited supply; here the target amount is amt = 11 (distinct from target amount 5 in Coin change II below and target amount 4 in the dynamic programming table). The goal is to find the minimum number of coins that sum to 11.
description: On the left, a table lists ID i and denomination coins[i - 1]; denomination 1 is shaded light orange and denomination 5 is shaded light green, sending arrows for 1 coin and 2 coins into the pouch on the right labeled "Target amount amt = 11". Denomination 2 is unused. The table below summarizes these highlights and arrows as coin counts.
At the bottom appear "Optimal coin combination: 1 + 5 + 5" and "Minimum number of coins: 3".

frames.title: Optimal coin combination for amount 11
frames.explanation: From the illustrated combination, 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 using 3 coins in total. Why 3 is minimal: because the largest denomination is 5, any two coins sum to at most 5 + 5 = 10 < 11, so fewer than 3 coins cannot reach 11 (derived from the input data rather than written in the figure).
